_README: Per-city copy for the service-area landing pages: /services/<trade>/<city>/. Each entry is the INTERSECTION of one trade and one city — what changes about that trade in that place — not the trade description repeated with a name swapped in, which would make these doorway pages. Jurisdiction claims match docs/service-area-verification.md, verified 2026-08-29. Build practice is UNVERIFIED: Quest must review and cut anything that does not match how it actually works. All fourteen trades are written now: roofing across all thirty-four cities, and the other thirteen across the twelve largest markets — one hundred and ninety pairings. A trade with no entry for a city simply has no page there, which is the point. Only the standalone site renders these; the ten demo directions do not carry them.

phoenix-az.lede: Phoenix spans a century of roofs, so the first question is never what it costs — it is what is actually up there.
paras: The centre of the city still has genuine low-slope roofs on pre-war and post-war houses, often built up in layers over decades and now carrying a foam coating that someone applied in the nineties. Out at the edges the same city is concrete tile over an underlayment laid in the 2000s. Those are different jobs with different failure modes, and quoting one as if it were the other is how a homeowner ends up with a surprise.

The recurring misunderstanding here is tile. Concrete tile lasts far longer than the felt beneath it, so a roof that looks sound from the street can be sitting on underlayment at the end of its life. We lift and stack the tile, replace what is underneath, and re-lay the same tile — a fraction of the cost of a tear-off, and the reason we always ask to look before pricing.
notes: City of Phoenix permit
Low-slope centre, tile at the edges
Tile relay over new underlayment

mesa-az.lede: Most of Mesa's roofs sit on post-war ranch and 1970s and 1980s block, and that vintage sets the work.
paras: Homes of that era were built with shallow pitches and long simple runs, which is good news — the tear-off is straightforward and there are few penetrations to detail around. What they do carry is decades of patch repairs around swamp coolers and later air-conditioning penetrations, and those patched areas are where a roof usually starts letting go rather than in the open field.

A City of Mesa reroof is its own permit, and we file it before anything comes off. Starting a tear-off against a permit that has not cleared is how a job ends up open to the sky waiting on paperwork — and in monsoon season that is not a theoretical risk.
notes: City of Mesa reroof permit
Post-war and 1970s block stock
Failures start at old penetrations

chandler-az.lede: Chandler's housing runs from the historic centre out to 2000s development, and its roofs divide on the same line.
paras: The bulk of the city is 1990s and 2000s concrete tile, and that stock has now reached the point where the underlayment beneath it is due even though the tile itself has decades left. A tile relay — lift, stack, replace the underlayment, re-lay — is the right answer far more often than a full replacement, and it is what we quote unless the tile is genuinely spent.

Nearer the historic centre the stock is older and lower-pitched, with more shingle and more previous repair. We scope those individually rather than assuming a Chandler address implies a particular roof, because the two halves of the city need different answers.
notes: City of Chandler permit
1990s–2000s tile at underlayment age
Older, lower-pitched near the centre

glendale-az.lede: Glendale splits sharply: shingle and low-slope around the older core, concrete tile out west.
paras: Around downtown and the historic districts the roofs are older and the constraints are tighter — a project inside a historic district is a different application, and what a roof is allowed to look like is a live question rather than a free choice. We settle material and colour with the city before ordering anything.

West of the 101 the stock is 1990s and 2000s tile on regular suburban lots, and the job there is almost always underlayment rather than tile. Mature ash and citrus over the older neighbourhoods also means leaf litter in valleys, which shortens the life of a roof in specific places rather than evenly.
notes: City of Glendale permit
Historic district material review
Leaf litter in valleys on older lots

scottsdale-az.lede: Scottsdale reviews what a roof looks like, not just whether it keeps water out.
paras: Design review here is genuinely enforced, and roof colour, profile and material are all part of it. We settle those on paper and get them approved before a pallet is ordered, because a roof delivered in a colour the city will not accept is an expensive mistake that is nobody's fault but the contractor's.

The stock itself is wide — high-end concrete and clay tile across much of the city, and low-slope foam on the contemporary desert houses where a parapet hides the roof entirely. Those flat roofs need a different specification and a different inspection rhythm from tile, and they are unforgiving about ponding where a drain has been added as an afterthought.
notes: City of Scottsdale design review
Colour and profile approved before ordering
Foam low-slope on contemporary houses

gilbert-az.lede: Gilbert is largely 1990s and 2000s master-planned, which means most of the town hit its first roof cycle at once.
paras: Concrete tile was standard across that build-out, and concrete tile outlives the felt beneath it by decades. What is failing across Gilbert now is underlayment, not tile — so the honest job is a relay: lift and stack the existing tile, strip and replace the underlayment, re-lay the tile with new fixings and replace only what broke in handling.

That distinction matters commercially. A homeowner told they need a new roof, when what they need is new underlayment under a perfectly good one, is being oversold. We quote the relay where the tile supports it and say plainly when it does not.
notes: Town of Gilbert permit
Underlayment failing, tile sound
Relay rather than replace

tempe-az.lede: Tempe is built out and tightly packed, so a reroof here is as much a logistics problem as a roofing one.
paras: Lots are small and neighbours are close. A tear-off generates noise, dust and a skip that has to go somewhere, and on many Tempe streets there is no somewhere. We plan the skip position, the loading window and the debris containment before the first tile moves, and we tell neighbours what is coming rather than letting them find out at seven in the morning.

The stock is mixed and mostly older than the outer valley — shallow pitches, previous repairs, and student-let properties where maintenance has been deferred for years. We expect to find more under a Tempe roof than under a suburban one, and we price the investigation honestly rather than discovering it halfway through.
notes: City of Tempe permit
Tight lots, planned skip and access
Deferred maintenance common

peoria-az.lede: Peoria runs a long way north to south, and its roofs get newer the further up you go.
paras: South Peoria is post-war and 1970s stock — shallower pitches, more shingle, more accumulated repair around penetrations. North of the 101 it is 1990s and 2000s tile in master-planned tracts, where the tile is fine and the underlayment is due.

The northern subdivisions add an HOA architectural committee on top of the city permit, and roof colour is exactly the sort of thing they rule on. We submit to both at the same time, because getting a city permit for a roof the HOA will reject wastes everybody's month.
notes: City of Peoria permit
HOA colour approval north of the 101
Older shingle south, tile north

surprise-az.lede: Almost every roof in Surprise went on after 1998, which makes the work unusually predictable.
paras: That means concrete tile over felt, laid within a few years of each other across whole neighbourhoods — and reaching the end of the underlayment's life at the same time. Streets here often see several relays in a season, and there is a real advantage in doing neighbouring houses together while the crew, the skip and the tile stacks are already on the street.

The age-restricted communities inside the city run their own architectural committees and their own contractor access hours. A seven-to-four window changes how many days a roof takes, and we build that into the programme rather than discovering it on day one.
notes: City of Surprise permit
Whole streets at underlayment age
Age-restricted access hours

avondale-az.lede: Avondale is mostly late-1990s and 2000s tile, with an older core that needs a different conversation.
paras: In the production tracts the tile is sound and the underlayment is the job. Lots are tight and side yards narrow, so the tile stacks and the skip have to be placed carefully — we would rather run a smaller machine and take an extra half day than take a fence down.
In the older core around historic Avondale the roofs are lower and more patched, often over block walls, and there is more variation house to house. Those we scope individually before quoting.
notes: City of Avondale permit
Tile relay in the production tracts
Narrow side-yard access

goodyear-az.lede: Goodyear's roofs are young, so most of what we do here is not replacement.
paras: Palm Valley, Estrella and the newer tracts are recent enough that the original tile and underlayment have life left. What brings us out is usually damage rather than age — wind lifting tile on an exposed elevation, a failed detail around a later solar installation, or a leak traced to a penetration cut after the roof went on.

Solar is worth naming. A great many Goodyear roofs have panels added years after the tile, and where the mounts were cut in badly they leak at the fixing rather than at the tile. Working around an array adds a day and a coordination call with the solar company, and we plan for both rather than pretending it is a normal roof.
notes: City of Goodyear permit
Damage and detailing over age
Solar array mounts and coordination

buckeye-az.lede: Buckeye has the newest roofs in the valley and the most exposed lots to put them on.
paras: Verrado, Sundance, Festival Ranch and the tracts around them are recent, so full replacement is rare. What is common is wind. The lots are open, there is little mature landscaping to break the weather, and the west-facing elevations take it directly — so lifted and slipped tile along ridges and rakes is the recurring call, along with the flashing details that go with it.

Buckeye is also geographically enormous. A roof on the far side of the city is a genuine drive for a crew and every delivery, so we bring materials in fewer larger loads and stage them on site rather than running back and forth.
notes: City of Buckeye permit
Wind lift on exposed elevations
Materials staged, not shuttled

queen-creek-az.lede: Queen Creek's lots are larger than the inner valley, and its roofs are mostly young.
paras: The town is primarily in Maricopa County but has extended into Pinal on its eastern and southern edges since the Ironwood Crossing annexation, so we confirm which side a property sits on before filing. The building permit itself is the town's either way.

The housing is largely 2000s and later tile, so underlayment is only now becoming the conversation on the earliest of it. More common are the outbuildings — shops, detached garages, ramadas and casitas on larger lots, which often carry metal or low-slope roofs that need a different specification from the house they sit behind.
notes: Town of Queen Creek permit
Maricopa and Pinal edges
Outbuildings with metal or low-slope roofs

maricopa-az.lede: The City of Maricopa is in Pinal County, and almost every roof in it went on after 2000.
paras: That means concrete tile in master-planned tracts — Rancho El Dorado, Province, Homestead — of an age where the tile is sound and the earliest underlayment is starting to come due. Relays rather than replacements, in other words, and whole streets reaching that point together.

It is far enough south of the valley that a crew is committed to the day once it arrives. We schedule Maricopa work in full days rather than half, and we stage everything on site, because a forgotten roll of underlayment is an hour each way.
notes: City of Maricopa permit, Pinal County
Post-2000 tile reaching underlayment age
Scheduled in full days

apache-junction-az.lede: Apache Junction has two roofing markets on the same streets, and they are not the same trade.
paras: Alongside conventional stick-built houses there is a large body of manufactured and mobile housing, park models and additions built onto them over decades. Roofing a manufactured home is a different discipline — different structure, different loading, different attachment, and often a roof-over rather than a tear-off. We are straight about what can and cannot sensibly be done to one rather than quoting it like a stick-built house.

The city issues the permit, and most of the city sits in Pinal County rather than Maricopa. Lots on the eastern edge rise towards the Superstitions with rock, slope and long unpaved approaches, which changes what a delivery truck can reach — we walk the access before quoting it.
notes: City of Apache Junction permit
Manufactured homes are a different trade
Access walked before quoting

el-mirage-az.lede: El Mirage divides between a small older core and the 2000s ring around it.
paras: In the core the roofs are older, lower and often over block, with more previous repair and more shingle. In the newer ring it is standard 2000s tile where underlayment is the coming job.

Lots in the older sections are compact and the streets narrow, so we keep the skip and the tile stacks inside the property line where we can. Blocking a street in a neighbourhood that tight makes the job everybody's problem, and it is avoidable with an hour of planning.
notes: City of El Mirage permit
Older core, 2000s ring
Skip and stacks kept off the street

fountain-hills-az.lede: Roofing in Fountain Hills is a hillside access problem before it is a roofing problem.
paras: Steep narrow streets, tight turnarounds and long driveways limit what can physically reach a house. A tear-off produces a great deal of debris that has to come down a grade, and a tile delivery has to get up one. We size the equipment and the loads to the driveway rather than the roof, and we walk it before we price it.

The houses themselves are largely custom and semi-custom from the 1990s and 2000s, stepped against the McDowells with complex roof geometry — more valleys, more hips, more transitions than a tract house. That is where the detailing work is, and where a cheap reroof shows itself within a season.
notes: Town of Fountain Hills permit
Grade limits deliveries and debris
Complex roof geometry, more detailing

litchfield-park-az.lede: Litchfield Park's mature canopy is the thing that decides when its roofs need work.
paras: Full-grown trees over a roof do two things: they drop litter into valleys where it holds moisture, and they shade parts of a roof unevenly. The result is that a Litchfield Park roof usually fails in specific places rather than all over — one bad elevation, one clogged valley — so a full replacement is often the wrong answer and a targeted repair is the right one.

The city runs design review and cares about the streetscape, so material and colour are settled with them rather than chosen off a board. On the older fabric around the Wigwam that matters more than it does in a newer suburb.
notes: City of Litchfield Park permit
Design review on material and colour
Uneven wear under mature canopy

tolleson-az.lede: Tolleson's housing is older and modest, and its roofs carry a lot of history.
paras: Small single-storey homes, block and frame, with decades of accumulated alterations — and a fair amount of roof work done at some point without a permit. We open things up and establish what is actually there before quoting, because a roof that has been patched over three times does not price like a clean tear-off.

The residential streets sit close to substantial distribution property, and the arterials around them carry heavy traffic at shift changes. We time material drops around that, because a delivery truck that cannot turn in is a wasted morning.
notes: City of Tolleson permit
Layered previous repairs
Deliveries timed around industrial traffic

youngtown-az.lede: Youngtown was built as a retirement community in the 1950s, and its roofs are all of a type.
paras: Compact single-storey houses with shallow pitches and low-slope sections, many now carrying coatings applied over older built-up roofing. Those coated low-slope roofs need a different specification from tile — they are unforgiving about ponding, and a coating applied over a substrate that was already failing buys a few years and hides the problem.

The lots are small and the roofs simple, which keeps the work quick and the cost sensible. It also means there is nowhere to put a skip except the front, so we plan the placement and keep the site clear at the end of each day.
notes: Town of Youngtown permit
1950s low-slope and shallow pitch
Coatings over failing substrate

wickenburg-az.lede: Wickenburg is ranch country, and roofing here includes buildings that are not houses.
paras: Barns, shops and outbuildings on acreage carry metal roofing far more often than tile, and metal is its own trade — panel selection, fastener pattern, thermal movement and flashing at every transition. We specify it as metal rather than treating it as a cheap alternative to a shingle roof.

In the historic downtown there is genuine old masonry and adobe, where a roof has to work with a wall that needs to breathe. An impermeable detail against an adobe parapet traps moisture in the wall, and that shows up years later as failed plaster rather than as a leak.
notes: Town of Wickenburg permit
Metal roofing on outbuildings
Breathable details on historic walls

carefree-az.lede: In Carefree what a roof looks like is regulated, and the town means it.
paras: Height, colour and how a building reads against the desert are all live questions, and roofs are part of that. Low-profile tile and concealed low-slope behind parapets are the norm rather than anything that announces itself, and dark-sky expectations rule out the reflective and the bright. We get the specification approved before ordering.

The houses are high-end custom on boulder lots, which makes access awkward and the finish standard unforgiving. Long clean runs and exposed detailing mean every fixing line is visible, so the setting-out matters more here than on a tract roof.
notes: Town of Carefree permit
Colour and profile reviewed
Boulder-lot access, visible detailing

cave-creek-az.lede: Cave Creek roofs sit on large rural lots, and the drive is part of the job.
paras: Long private approaches, desert ground and rock close to the surface all limit what a loaded truck can do. We stage materials once and work from the stack rather than shuttling, and we protect the desert we drive over rather than making a new track across it.

The houses are largely custom with substantial roof areas and real wind exposure on open ground. Ridge and rake detailing takes the weather here in a way it does not in a sheltered subdivision, and that is where we spend the extra time.
notes: Town of Cave Creek permit
Long approaches, staged materials
Wind exposure at ridges and rakes

paradise-valley-az.lede: Paradise Valley governs building on its own terms, and roofs are no exception.
paras: The town reviews height, and on a large single-storey house the roof is what determines it. Material, profile and colour are all part of what will actually be permitted, so a Paradise Valley roof starts with the town rather than with a sample board. We settle it on paper first.

The houses are large custom builds, often with complex low-slope and tile combinations, deep overhangs and concealed drainage. Those hidden gutters and internal drains are where the expensive failures happen — not on the open field of the roof — and they are what we inspect first.
notes: Town of Paradise Valley permit
Roof drives the height review
Concealed drainage is the failure point

guadalupe-az.lede: Guadalupe is dense and tightly built, and roofing here is close-quarters work.
paras: Small lots, single storey, block and frame with decades of self-built additions layered on — and those additions are usually where a roof leaks, at the junction between what was original and what was added later. We establish what is actually there before quoting rather than after.

The streets are narrow and parking is tight. We keep the working footprint inside the property line, run smaller equipment, and close the site up at the end of each day rather than leaving materials out overnight.
notes: Town of Guadalupe permit
Leaks at original-to-addition junctions
Contained site on narrow streets

laveen-az.lede: Laveen is mostly 2000s tract housing, and its roofs are reaching their first real service point.
paras: Concrete tile over felt, laid across large subdivisions within a few years of each other, now old enough that the underlayment is the coming job while the tile itself is fine. A relay is usually the right answer here, and we say so.

Work inside the Phoenix city limits permits through the city. Laveen's southern edge runs against the Gila River Indian Community, which is sovereign ground with its own building safety and its own adopted codes — a property the far side of that line is not a Phoenix permit at all, and we establish which side a parcel sits on first.
notes: City of Phoenix permit
2000s tile at underlayment age
Tribal jurisdiction to the south

sun-city-az.lede: Sun City's roofs are unlike anything else in the valley, and most valley roofers price them wrong.
paras: The original 1960s and 1970s housing is compact, single-storey and largely low-slope — built-up roofing, later foam and coatings, on shallow decks with carports attached. These are not tile roofs and they do not behave like tile roofs. They fail by ponding, by coating breakdown and at parapet and scupper details, and they need a specification written for low slope rather than a pitched-roof product applied optimistically.

There are two permits here, not one. Sun City is unincorporated, so the building permit is a Maricopa County submittal — and the Sun City Fire District issues its own permit and inspections for fire and life safety alongside it. Missing the second one stops a job.
notes: Maricopa County permit
Separate Sun City Fire District permit
Low-slope built-up and coated roofs

sun-city-west-az.lede: Sun City West is a generation newer than Sun City, and its roofs are a different problem.
paras: Development began in 1978, so the stock here is larger, on larger lots, with pitched tile roofs rather than the low-slope build-ups of original Sun City. The two communities are constantly confused and they do not need the same work — here the job is usually underlayment beneath sound tile.

Like Sun City it is unincorporated, so the permit is a Maricopa County submittal rather than a city one. As an age-restricted community it also sets expectations on access, noise and working hours, and we plan the programme around them.
notes: Maricopa County permit
Pitched tile, not low-slope
Community access and hours

san-tan-valley-az.lede: San Tan Valley's roofs are young; its permitting is the part that needs attention.
paras: The town incorporated on 1 July 2026 and permitting is mid-handover. Until the changeover completes it is two steps — a zoning clearance from the Town, then the building permit from Pinal County with that clearance attached. We confirm which path is live at the time of the job rather than assuming, because it is genuinely moving.

The housing itself is overwhelmingly 2000s and later tile in master-planned tracts, so full replacement is rare. Exposure is the issue: open lots with little mature landscaping mean wind gets at ridges and rakes, and that is where the repair calls come from.
notes: Town clearance, Pinal County permit
2000s tile, rarely replaced
Wind at ridges on open lots

anthem-az.lede: Anthem sits high enough that its roofs take weather the valley floor does not.
paras: Colder nights, more wind and real monsoon activity mean flashing, ridge detail and fixing schedules need specifying for this elevation rather than for central Phoenix. A detail that is adequate in Chandler is not automatically adequate here, and the difference shows up in a bad season.

Anthem is unincorporated, so the building permit is a Maricopa County submittal. Both the Country Club side and Parkside run active architectural committees, and roof colour is exactly what they rule on — we submit to the committee and the county together rather than in sequence.
notes: Maricopa County permit
HOA colour approval both sides
Detailing specified for elevation

deer-valley-az.lede: Deer Valley's housing is 1980s to 2000s, which puts most of it at its first roof replacement.
paras: Homes of that age reach a point where the roof covering, the water heater and the electrical panel all come due within a few years of each other. Planning those together is cheaper than doing them separately, and a roof is the one that decides the sequence — nobody wants a new panel installed under a roof about to be torn off.

Work here permits through the City of Phoenix. Parts of the village sit under the Deer Valley Airport Overlay, a named district in the city's zoning ordinance rather than an informal noise zone, and it carries requirements of its own worth knowing before drawings are started.
notes: City of Phoenix permit
First replacement cycle
Deer Valley Airport Overlay district

north-phoenix-az.lede: North Phoenix is a colloquial name covering a wide range of roofs and two different permit paths.
paras: The housing spans 1970s block through current build. A 1970s roof here means shallow pitch, previous repair and probably a swamp cooler penetration someone patched around; a 2005 roof means tile with underlayment coming due. We scope rather than assume, because the same phrase covers both.

Most of what people mean by North Phoenix sits inside the city and permits through Phoenix, but the northern fringe runs out into unincorporated Maricopa County where the permit is a county submittal instead. The two processes and timelines are not the same, so we confirm the parcel before quoting.
notes: City of Phoenix, or county at the fringe
1970s block through current build
Scoped, not assumed

south-phoenix-az.lede: South Phoenix has some of the oldest roofs in the city and a jurisdiction line that matters.
paras: Pre-war and post-war houses on large irregular lots, some originally agricultural, alongside recent infill. The older properties often carry additions built over decades without paperwork, and the roof junctions between original and addition are where the water gets in. We establish what is there and what is legally there before designing anything on top of it.

The parts inside the city limits permit through Phoenix. South and west the ground becomes the Gila River Indian Community — sovereign, with its own building safety and its own adopted code editions. That boundary decides who issues the permit and which code the roof is built to, so it is the first thing we check.
notes: City of Phoenix inside city limits
Tribal jurisdiction south and west
Leaks at unpermitted addition junctions

ahwatukee-az.lede: Ahwatukee was built out through the 1980s and 1990s, and its roofs are all arriving together.
paras: Tile over felt across most of the village, laid in a concentrated period, and now well into the range where underlayment is the job rather than the tile. Whole streets reach that point in the same few years, and there is a real saving in doing neighbouring houses while the crew and the skip are already there.

Most of the village sits inside an HOA that reviews roof colour and material, and that approval is as much a gate as the city permit. Work permits through the City of Phoenix — Ahwatukee is a Phoenix urban village, not a separate town, whatever it feels like from the far side of South Mountain.
notes: City of Phoenix permit
HOA colour and material review
Whole streets at underlayment age

phoenix-az.lede: Phoenix concrete is mostly replacement, and what comes out tells you what has to go back in.
paras: Older Phoenix drives and patios were poured thin, often without reinforcement, and decades of ground movement and tree roots show up as lifted panels and cracks that run corner to corner. We take out enough to see what the sub-base is doing rather than pouring over the problem, because a slab is only ever as flat as the ground under it stays.

In the historic districts the drive and the walk are street-facing, so the finish carries as much weight as the strength. We match panel layout and joint pattern to what is already there instead of imposing a modern broom finish on a 1920s frontage, and where the work runs out toward the street we settle what the city wants before anything is saw-cut.
notes: Thin, unreinforced older slabs
Sub-base read before the surface
Street-facing work in historic districts

mesa-az.lede: Mesa's post-war lots came with narrow drives and thin patios, and most of our work here widens them.
paras: A ranch-era drive was poured for one car and no truck: four inches of unreinforced concrete on whatever was under it in 1958. Widening one means matching the height of the old panel, tying the two together properly and reinforcing the new pour, or the seam parts company in the first hot summer and you have two slabs instead of one.

Mesa runs its own Development Services, so where the work touches the structure or the street it is a City of Mesa submittal rather than a county one and the review window goes into the programme up front. Colour and texture will never match a fifty-year-old slab exactly. We say that at the quote rather than promising an invisible join.
notes: Widening ranch-era drives
City of Mesa submittal
Honest about matching an old pour

chandler-az.lede: Chandler asks for more patio than it asks for repair, and the two jobs start in different places.
paras: Most of what we pour in Chandler extends something that already works: a patio pushed out to cover a west-facing door, a pad for an outdoor kitchen, a walk tying a side gate to a new one. On sound 1990s and 2000s slabs the existing pour is a good datum, so the work is layout, fall and joint placement rather than demolition.

Where a slab has cracked we look for the reason before quoting a replacement. A crack running out of a re-entrant corner is a control-joint problem rather than a failure, and grinding, sealing and cutting the joint that should have been there is often the honest answer. If the sub-base has moved we say so, because the same slab poured back on the same ground does the same thing again.
notes: Extensions on sound slabs
Cracks read before they are quoted
Joints cut where they belong

gilbert-az.lede: Gilbert's slabs are the same age as its roofs, and the builder details repeat street to street.
paras: A 1990s or 2000s Gilbert subdivision was poured by one builder to one detail, so the cracking on one elevation is usually the cracking on the next. That works in a homeowner's favour: we can generally say what a drive or a patio needs without exploratory demolition, because we have cut the same slab on the same street before.

Anything visible from the street goes past the community's architectural committee, and colour, finish and banding all count as visible. We work from what is approved for that community and put it in alongside the Town of Gilbert paperwork rather than pouring first and finding the palette afterwards.
notes: One builder, one detail, one fix
Finish approved by the committee
Town of Gilbert paperwork

glendale-az.lede: Glendale's older lots still flood-irrigate, and that decides when a slab can be poured at all.
paras: A yard that takes four inches of water on an irrigation turn is not a yard to pour into on a whim. We book the pour against the turn, protect the sub-base and set the fall so the finished slab sheds toward where the water is meant to go rather than damming it against the house.

Mature ash and citrus over an old drive means roots under it, and roots are why so many Glendale panels have lifted. Cutting one out and pouring it back without dealing with what raised it buys about two years. Beyond the 101 the ground is newer, the slabs are sound, and the work is extension rather than repair.
notes: Poured around the irrigation turn
Root lift on older panels
Extension work west of the 101

scottsdale-az.lede: In Scottsdale a slab is a drainage decision before it is a concrete one.
paras: Hillside and desert-adjacent lots move water in a particular direction, and every impermeable surface added to one changes where it goes. Falls, kerbs and any retention are set against the existing grade at design stage rather than discovered in the first storm, and on a hillside lot the disturbed area is planned rather than assumed.

Scottsdale reviews what a thing looks like, not only whether it works. Finish, colour and joint layout are settled and submitted before anyone books a truck, because a rejected finish is a great deal cheaper on paper than it is on nine hundred square feet of cured concrete.
notes: Falls and retention set at design
Disturbed area planned on hillside lots
Finish approved before the pour

tempe-az.lede: In Tempe the concrete is the straightforward part and getting it to the back of the lot is not.
paras: Lots here are small, neighbours are close and a mixer often cannot reach the pour. Where an alley gives us access we use it; where it does not, the pump, the barrow route and the protection that goes with them are planned before the truck is booked, because a pour that stalls halfway is a cold joint somebody lives with permanently.

Much of the older stock has been worked on more than once, so what sits under an existing patio is genuinely unknown until it is out: old footings, a filled-in cooler pad, occasionally the slab of an addition nobody permitted. That gets allowed for at the quote rather than found with a saw already in the ground.
notes: Alley access where it exists
Pump and barrow planned, not improvised
Unknown ground under old patios

peoria-az.lede: Peoria's concrete work changes at the 101: replacement to the south of it, addition to the north.
paras: South Peoria's drives and walks are post-war and 1970s, poured thin and now carrying tree roots and settlement, so the work there starts with what the sub-base is doing. North of the 101 the slabs are recent and sound, and the job is what the production builder left out — a patio extension, an RV pad, a walk down to a casita.

The northern subdivisions bring an architectural committee on top of the City of Peoria permit, and a poured surface visible from the street is theirs to approve. We submit both in parallel rather than one after the other, because finding the committee once the city has already signed off is how a schedule loses a month.
notes: Replacement south, extension north
City of Peoria permitting
Committee and city submitted in parallel

surprise-az.lede: Almost every slab in Surprise went down after 1998, so the work is addition rather than repair.
paras: A twenty-year-old production slab is usually sound, which makes the work predictable: extend the patio, pour the pad for a casita, run the side walk the builder never platted. The craft problem is the join — matching level, colour and joint pattern to a slab that has been curing and fading in the sun for two decades.

Inside Sun City Grand and the other age-restricted communities the working hours and contractor access are set by the community rather than by us. A pour is not a job that can start at ten and stop at four without consequence, so the pour day is planned around those windows before it is quoted.
notes: Post-1998 slabs, sound to build on
Matching a twenty-year-old pour
Pour day planned to access hours

goodyear-az.lede: Goodyear's ground moves in places, and a slab that ignores that cracks on schedule.
paras: Expansive soil on the south and west edges of the city swells and shrinks with moisture, and a patio or a casita pad poured onto it without thought cracks along a predictable line. We set finished floor and fall against the existing grade at design stage, keep water moving away from the slab edge, and reinforce for the ground that is actually there.

Most of what we pour here is outdoor living on production homes that are otherwise sound: extended patios, ramada footings, kitchen pads. All of it lands against an existing slab, so the join, the level and the way the two shed water matter more than the concrete itself.
notes: Expansive soil at the city edges
Fall set before the pour
Ramada and outdoor-kitchen pads

queen-creek-az.lede: Queen Creek's lots are big enough that the concrete is often a drive's length from the house.
paras: Shops, extended garages and RV pads are a large share of what we pour here, and on a lot this size the access drive is a structure rather than an apron. Thickness, reinforcement and sub-base have to carry a loaded truck rather than a saloon car, so it is specified for what will genuinely drive on it.

Parcels toward the edges of town can still be on well and septic, and a leach field is not something to find with a saw. Services are located and the pour set around them before we quote, because a hundred and fifty feet of trench or a relocated line is a line item and not a rounding error.
notes: Drives specified for loaded trucks
Septic and well located first
Shop and RV pads on larger lots

buckeye-az.lede: Buckeye's slabs are the newest we work on, and nearly all of them are being extended for shade.
paras: Verrado, Sundance and the Festival Ranch tracts were platted open, and a west-facing patio out here is unusable for a third of the year. Most of our concrete is the footing and pad under something that casts a shadow — a ramada, a pergola, an extended cover — so it is set out for the structure going on top of it rather than poured and drilled into afterwards.

The city is geographically enormous and a pour on the far side of it is a real drive for every truck. We book the concrete in fewer, larger loads, stage what can be staged on site, and set the day around the delivery window instead of running the road four times.
notes: Footings set out for the structure
Shade first, surface second
Fewer, larger deliveries

phoenix-az.lede: Phoenix stucco runs from original render on 1920s walls to 2010s three-coat over frame.
paras: Those are not the same material and they do not want the same repair. Render on a masonry or lath wall breathes and moves differently from a modern three-coat over board, and patching one with the other traps moisture and opens along the join inside a season. We work out what is actually on the wall before quoting what goes back onto it.

Street-facing elevations in the historic districts carry real value in their texture and detail, and a sprayed finish flattened over a hand-floated one is the quickest way to lose it. Texture is matched by sample on the wall itself rather than from a chart, and what should be kept is kept.
notes: Original render and modern three-coat
Matched by sample on the wall
Street-facing detail in historic districts

mesa-az.lede: Matching a Mesa wall that has weathered forty years is a different job from finishing it new.
paras: Stucco over block moves and weathers differently from stucco over frame, and most of Mesa's post-war and 1970s stock is the former. Four decades of sun has taken the colour down and rounded the texture, so a patch mixed to the original recipe still reads as a patch. We float sample areas and let the owner see them on the wall before an elevation is committed.

Cracking over block is usually telling you about a lintel or a joint rather than about the render, so we look at what is behind it before anything is recoated. Where the repair reaches the structure it becomes a City of Mesa submittal, and that gets settled before scaffold goes up rather than after.
notes: Stucco over block, not frame
Samples floated on the wall
Cracks read as a wall problem

chandler-az.lede: Most Chandler elevations we are called to need preparation and a recoat, not replacement.
paras: The stucco on a 1990s or 2000s Chandler house is usually sound underneath a faded, chalked surface. Where that is what we find we say so: wash it, repair the cracks properly, prime what needs priming and recoat. Quoting a full re-stucco on a wall that does not need one is easy money, and we would rather keep the customer.

The cracks that do matter are the ones repeating in the same place — over a window head, out of a re-entrant corner, along a control joint that was never cut. Those are treated as a detail problem before anything is coated, because a fresh finish over an unresolved crack cracks again on the same line inside a year.
notes: Recoat where a recoat will do
Repeating cracks treated as details
Preparation is most of the job

gilbert-az.lede: In Gilbert the colour is largely decided for you, which makes stucco a matching exercise.
paras: Elevations in a Gilbert community were built to an approved palette, so the question is rarely which colour but which of the approved ones this house already is. Twenty years of sun means the swatch on file and the wall in front of you are no longer the same thing. We match to the wall and take that to the committee rather than the other way round.

Production three-coat over frame fails in predictable places on this stock: at the corners of openings, where foam trim meets the field, and along the line of a party wall on an attached elevation. Because the builder detail repeats down the street, we usually know what we are looking at before the scaffold is up.
notes: Approved palette, faded wall
Matched to the wall, not the swatch
Predictable cracking at openings

glendale-az.lede: Glendale has pre-war render downtown and 2000s stucco west of the 101, and they want different hands.
paras: Around the older core there is genuine pre-war and post-war fabric, some of it on raised foundations, and a project inside one of the historic districts is a different application from the same job three streets away. Original render is usually worth repairing rather than covering, and what a street-facing elevation ends up looking like is part of that conversation.

Flood irrigation on the older lots matters to stucco more than people expect. Standing water at the base of a wall wicks up and takes the finish off from the bottom, so grade and splash at the base are dealt with as part of the repair rather than coated over to fail again on the next turn.
notes: Historic district rules downtown
Repair before recoat on old render
Wicking at the base on irrigated lots

scottsdale-az.lede: Scottsdale approves the colour and the finish before the wall is allowed either.
paras: Design review here is genuinely enforced, so material, texture and colour are settled and submitted before a crew is booked. On the contemporary houses the parapet and reveal detailing is as much of the job as the field is, and a reveal out by a quarter of an inch stays visible from the street for the life of the building.

West-facing elevations on desert-adjacent lots take punishing exposure, and a dark colour on a hot wall moves. Finish and colour are specified against that exposure rather than chosen from a showroom sample under fluorescent light, and we say when a selection will not hold up where it is going.
notes: Colour and finish approved first
Parapet and reveal detailing
West elevations specified for exposure

tempe-az.lede: On a Tempe lot the neighbour's car is eight feet from the wall being sprayed.
paras: Masking, overspray and dust control are part of the plan here rather than an afterthought, because the lots are small and everything is close to everything. Working hours are agreed, what is next door is protected and the street stays passable — worth doing on its own merits, and also the difference between a job that finishes and one that collects complaints.

Much of the stock around the university has spent years as rental, and the walls carry patching from a run of earlier owners: three colours under the current one, a hand-floated repair next to a troweled flat one. We open enough to see how many layers are on the wall before quoting, because that is what decides between a recoat and a strip.
notes: Overspray and dust planned for
Layered patching under the top coat
Working hours agreed with neighbours

peoria-az.lede: Peoria's stucco is over block in the south of the city and over frame in the north.
paras: That difference decides the repair. Render on 1970s block moves with the masonry and fails around lintels and joints; three-coat over frame on a newer elevation fails at the corners of openings and where trim meets the field. The wall tells us which conversation we are having well before a price does.

North of the 101 the community architectural committee has a view on colour, and the elevation has faded away from whatever is on file with them. We match to the wall, take that to the committee alongside the City of Peoria paperwork, and get both moving at once rather than in sequence.
notes: Block in the south, frame in the north
Failure points differ by build
Colour matched, then approved

surprise-az.lede: In Surprise the stucco question is how to make new work disappear into a twenty-year-old wall.
paras: Nearly everything here went up after 1998 to a consistent recipe — three-coat over frame in one of a handful of textures — and that consistency is an advantage on an addition, because the recipe is knowable. What cannot be reproduced from a chart is two decades of sun, so samples are floated on the actual elevation and agreed before the field goes on.

Where an addition ties into an existing wall we plan the break at a natural line: a corner, a reveal, a change of plane. A join stopped in the middle of a flat elevation will find the light eventually, whatever it looked like on the day it was floated.
notes: Consistent post-1998 three-coat
Samples floated on the real wall
Joins planned at natural breaks

goodyear-az.lede: In Goodyear a stucco crack is often the ground talking rather than the render failing.
paras: Expansive soil in parts of the city moves a slab enough to telegraph into the wall above it, and that shows as diagonal cracking out of the corners of openings rather than as random crazing across a field. Recoating over it hides the symptom until the next wet season, so we look at the shape of the crack before deciding whether this is a stucco job at all.

The rest is younger production work where the render is sound and the elevation has simply gone chalky in the sun. That is preparation, proper crack repair and a recoat — and where a wall needs only that, we say so instead of quoting the larger job.
notes: Diagonal cracks read as movement
Recoat where the render is sound
Younger production elevations

queen-creek-az.lede: Queen Creek stucco is usually about making a new shop or casita look like it came with the house.
paras: On lots this size an outbuilding is a building in its own right, and it either matches the house or announces itself permanently. We take texture and colour off the existing elevation, float samples against it, and finish the new structure to the house rather than to a spec sheet.

Much of this housing is new enough that the original builder may still carry some of it. Where a crack or a delamination looks like original workmanship we say so plainly rather than quietly repairing something somebody else owes.
notes: Outbuildings finished to the house
Texture taken off the existing wall
Builder coverage sorted honestly

buckeye-az.lede: Buckeye's elevations are new, open, and facing the sun with nothing standing in the way.
paras: With no mature trees and few neighbouring rooflines to break the light, a west or south wall out here takes as much exposure as anything we work on. Colour choice is a durability decision as much as a taste one, and we will say when a dark selection is going to fade unevenly on the elevation it is going onto.

The stock is recent enough that failures are detailing rather than age: where render meets a window flange, where a patio cover or ramada has been fixed back into the wall, where an earlier trade cut in and patched it flat. Those are repaired as details rather than buried under a fresh field coat.
notes: Exposure decides the colour
Detail failures, not age
Patches around later fixings

phoenix-az.lede: A Phoenix ADU is decided by the lot a long time before it is decided by the plan.
paras: Setbacks, where the existing house sits on the plot and where the services already run tend to fix where a second dwelling can go before anyone picks a layout. We survey and confirm what is allowed on that particular parcel before drawings start, because a design drawn to the wrong envelope is time nobody gets back.

On the older central lots the utilities are as old as the house. Panel capacity, the condition of the sewer line and the route it takes are what decide whether a build is straightforward or expensive, and they are worth establishing at the outset rather than once a trench is already open.
notes: Envelope confirmed before drawings
Panel and sewer checked early
Older lots, older services

mesa-az.lede: Mesa's post-war lots are deep, and most of them have room behind the house for a second dwelling.
paras: A ranch lot with a long back yard is close to ideal: room to set the building well away from the house, a side gate wide enough to get materials through, and services already run to the back for a cooler or a shed. We check that access before anything else, because a build a machine cannot reach is a build done by hand.

The paperwork goes to City of Mesa Development Services, and out in the east Mesa subdivisions there is an HOA architectural review sitting on top of it. Both go in together. Matching a new elevation to stucco that has weathered forty years is the part that takes craft rather than paperwork.
notes: Deep lots, room behind the house
Access checked before design
City and HOA submitted together

chandler-az.lede: Most Chandler ADU conversations start with a family member rather than with a rental.
paras: Ageing parents, an adult child, a home office that has outgrown a bedroom — that is what is being built here, and it changes the brief. A unit a family will actually live in wants a proper kitchen, level access and a bathroom that still works in fifteen years, not the smallest thing that meets a definition.

Chandler lots from the 1990s and 2000s were platted with the yard at the back and the services down one side, so the practical question is how far the new building sits from the existing sewer and panel. Those runs are priced at the start, because they move the number more than the finishes do.
notes: Built for family, not for turnover
Level access and a real kitchen
Service runs priced at the start

gilbert-az.lede: In Gilbert an ADU has to satisfy the town and the community, and they ask different questions.
paras: The town looks at the envelope, the services and the structure. The architectural committee looks at what the neighbours will see: roof pitch, tile, colour, and how a new elevation sits against the approved palette. We work both at once and design to the palette from the outset rather than redrawing after a rejection.

Because these subdivisions were built by one builder to a controlled set of elevations, a well-matched casita reads as though it came with the house. That is the standard worth aiming at here, with the tile, the fascia line and the stucco texture all taken off the existing building.
notes: Town envelope, committee appearance
Designed to the approved palette
Matched tile, fascia and texture

glendale-az.lede: Glendale's older lots have the space for an ADU and the complications of an old yard with it.
paras: Mature trees, flood irrigation and a raised original foundation all bear on where a second dwelling can sit and how its floor level is set. We survey grade and the irrigation route first, because a building placed across the way water moves through a yard causes a problem every time the turn comes round.

Inside a historic district what can be seen from the street is part of the application even when the new building is at the back. West of the 101 the lots are 1990s and 2000s production and the questions are the ordinary ones: setbacks, coverage, and where the services already run.
notes: Grade and irrigation surveyed first
Historic districts see the street
Ordinary envelope questions west of the 101

scottsdale-az.lede: Scottsdale wants to see what an ADU will look like as well as where it is going to sit.
paras: Documentation is the job here. Elevations, materials and colours are settled and submitted before anything is ordered, and on a hillside lot the drainage, the limits on what ground may be disturbed and how the building steps with the slope belong to the same conversation. That work happens on paper, which is where it is cheap.

Central and south Scottsdale's older ranch lots are generous and often take a casita comfortably. Further north the committees are stricter and the palette is controlled, so the design becomes a matching exercise against the existing house rather than an opportunity to do something different.
notes: Documented design review
Hillside grade and drainage
Matching palette further north

tempe-az.lede: Tempe is built out, so an ADU here is usually a conversion, an alley plot, or nothing.
paras: Lots are small and the setbacks eat into them quickly, which is why so many of these projects are conversions rather than new buildings — a garage brought up to a habitable standard, or a compact unit where an alley already provides the access. Which of those a lot actually supports is worth settling before anything is drawn.

Converting an older structure means finding what earlier owners did to it: circuits added without permit, a slab never poured to carry a wall, insulation that was never there at all. We open enough to know before quoting, because the discovery is the part that moves the price.
notes: Conversion more often than new build
Alley access where it exists
Earlier unpermitted work found first

peoria-az.lede: Peoria's ADU work sits north of the 101, where the lots were platted with room to spare.
paras: The northern subdivisions were laid out with side yards and rear space the production builder never used, and a casita is the obvious thing to put there. The architectural committee will have a view, so roof, tile and colour are matched to the house and taken to them alongside the City of Peoria submittal.

South of the 101 the lots are older and tighter and the answer is more often a conversion or an addition than a separate building. Either way the deciding factors are the same: setbacks, the capacity of the panel, and how far the sewer is from where a new bathroom wants to be.
notes: Room to build north of the 101
Committee and city in parallel
Conversion more likely in the south

surprise-az.lede: Plenty of Surprise lots were platted with room for a casita that was never actually built.
paras: That is a good place to start from: the space is there, the ground is flat, the services are modern and the existing structure is sound. The work becomes siting it well — far enough from the house to feel separate, close enough that the sewer and power runs stay sensible — and finishing it so it does not read as an afterthought.

In the age-restricted communities the rules on occupancy of a second dwelling, on contractor access and on working hours are set by the community. We read them before quoting, because they shape both what can be built and how long it takes to build it.
notes: Lots platted with the room
Siting balanced against service runs
Community rules read before quoting

goodyear-az.lede: Goodyear casitas are common enough that the lots were often laid out expecting one.
paras: Palm Valley, Estrella and the newer tracts have the space and the services, so the technical questions here are ground and drainage rather than structure. Expansive soil in parts of the city means the pad is designed for the ground it is actually on, and finished floor and fall are set against existing grade before anything is poured.

Matching matters as much as building does. Tile profile, fascia line, stucco texture and colour all come off the existing house, because a casita that is nearly right is more noticeable than one that is obviously new.
notes: Space and services already there
Pad designed for the ground
Finished to the existing house

queen-creek-az.lede: On a Queen Creek acre an ADU is easy to place, and the services are the hard part.
paras: Where a parcel is on well and septic, a second dwelling is a question about the system before it is a question about the building: what the existing field was sized for, where it sits, and what a second bathroom does to it. We establish that early, because the answer occasionally changes the project.

On the larger lots the run from house to casita can be a hundred and fifty feet or more of trench for water, waste and power. That is a real line item, surveyed and priced before we quote rather than after, along with the access a machine needs to get back there at all.
notes: Septic capacity established first
Long service runs priced, not assumed
Access for machinery planned

buckeye-az.lede: Buckeye lots have the room for a casita and none of the shade to put it in.
paras: Orientation does more work here than almost anywhere else in the valley. A second dwelling with its glazing facing west is expensive to cool for the life of the building, so we site and orient it for the sun first and the view second, and the covered space between the two buildings is designed rather than left over.

The tracts are recent, the ground is generally straightforward and the services are modern, which keeps the build itself predictable. What is not predictable is the drive: the city is enormous, so deliveries are consolidated and staged on site instead of run in daily.
notes: Sited and oriented for the sun
Modern services, predictable build
Deliveries consolidated and staged

phoenix-az.lede: A Phoenix remodel starts with the age of the house, because that decides what is behind the wall.
paras: A 1920s bungalow has lath and plaster, original framing and a panel that was never meant to carry a modern kitchen. A 2005 house has drywall, trusses and capacity to spare. Demolition, dust control and the electrical scope are different in each, and pretending otherwise is how a fixed price turns into a run of variations.

In the historic districts the inside of the house is generally the owner's business while the street-facing exterior is not, so we are clear from the start about which parts of a project attract that scrutiny and which do not. Where original interior detail is worth keeping, we plan to keep it rather than clearing it because clearing is quicker.
notes: Age decides what is behind the wall
Panel capacity priced up front
Original detail kept where it matters

mesa-az.lede: In a Mesa block house, which walls can come out is the first question a remodel has to answer.
paras: Painted masonry is not a stud wall to be opened with a sledgehammer and a header off the shelf. On post-war and 1970s Mesa stock we establish what is structural, what is infill and what a real opening will take before a layout is promised, because a kitchen drawn without that is a picture rather than a plan.

Original branch circuits in that stock usually need bringing up to current code once the walls are open, and that is a City of Mesa submittal with a review window inside it. It goes into the programme at the start rather than being discovered halfway through demolition.
notes: Block walls established before layout
Circuits brought up when walls open
City of Mesa review in the programme

chandler-az.lede: Chandler remodels usually start from a sound house whose finishes have simply dated.
paras: That is a favourable starting point and it changes the conversation. With the structure and the services in reasonable order, the work is about layout, storage and light rather than repair — which is where the budget should be going in any case.

Most of these houses are lived in throughout the job. We stage the work so a family keeps a working kitchen or bathroom for as long as it possibly can, seal the working area properly, and keep the run from the front door to the skip off the carpet. None of that is glamorous and all of it is what people remember.
notes: Sound structure, dated finishes
Layout, storage and light
Staged around a family living in it

gilbert-az.lede: Gilbert's original kitchens went in with the houses, and a town's worth reached the end together.
paras: A 1990s or 2000s builder kitchen was specified to a price: particleboard boxes, a laminate top and a soffit dropped over the wall cabinets to save on door heights. Taking that soffit out is usually the single change that transforms the room, and because the detail repeats down the street we generally know what is inside it before it comes down.

Interior work is between the homeowner and the town rather than the architectural committee, whose interest begins at the elevation. That is worth knowing at the outset: an interior remodel can move at the pace of the permit instead of the pace of a monthly meeting.
notes: Builder kitchens at end of life
Soffits out, ceiling height recovered
No committee on interior work

glendale-az.lede: Glendale remodels split by age: wiring behind lath downtown, drywall and trusses out west.
paras: Around the older core, opening a wall means finding out how many times the house has been rewired and how much of the original is still live. Some of that stock sits on raised floors as well, which changes plumbing runs entirely. We survey enough to price honestly rather than quoting the visible work and discovering the rest with the walls open.

Newer Glendale, out beyond the 101, is production-built and predictable, and the work there is reconfiguration: taking out the wall between kitchen and family room, turning an oversized garden bath into a shower and storage somebody will actually use.
notes: Original wiring behind lath downtown
Raised floors change plumbing runs
Reconfiguration in the newer west

scottsdale-az.lede: A Scottsdale remodel lives or dies on the finish schedule being settled before anything is ordered.
paras: Long lead times on cabinetry, stone and tile mean the decisions have to be made early and then held. We settle the schedule, order against it and sequence the trades to it, because a change of mind at week six is a change to the programme rather than to a line item.

The older ranch stock in central and south Scottsdale takes reconfiguration well — the wall between kitchen and living space is rarely load-bearing on those plans, and opening it transforms a house without extending it. Which walls are structural gets confirmed before the drawing rather than after it.
notes: Finish schedule settled and held
Long lead times sequenced
Ranch plans open up well

tempe-az.lede: In Tempe you routinely find a bathroom that was redone three times before you got there.
paras: A great deal of the stock here has been rental for years and carries layered work from earlier owners, some of it done without permit. Opening it up means finding what was buried: circuits added without inspection, waste that was never vented properly, a floor built up three times to bury the last problem. We price that discovery honestly instead of pretending a wall will open clean.

Lots are small and neighbours are close, so dust control, the skip position and working hours are part of the plan rather than an afterthought. On an infill street there is nowhere to put a mess, which means the site has to be tidy at the end of every day rather than at the end of the job.
notes: Layered work from earlier owners
Discovery priced, not assumed away
Nowhere to put a mess on an infill lot

peoria-az.lede: Peoria's remodels get simpler the further north you go, and the reason is usually the wiring.
paras: South Peoria's post-war and 1970s stock brings the electrical and mechanical upgrades that come with opening those walls: original branch circuits, a panel sized for a different era, ducting routed for a swamp cooler. That work is real and it belongs in the price at the beginning rather than in a variation later.

North of the 101 the houses are recent and sound, and the work is finishing what the production builder did not: an island that was never plumbed, a laundry that needs to work harder, a bathroom reconfigured out of the standard plan. It is a City of Peoria submittal at either end of the city.
notes: Electrical upgrades in the older south
Finishing production plans in the north
City of Peoria submittal either end

surprise-az.lede: Much of the remodelling in Surprise is a bathroom being made to work for the next twenty years.
paras: In the age-restricted communities the brief is often level access, a walk-in shower, better light, and blocking in the walls for rails that may not be wanted yet. That is detail work rather than structural work, and it wants doing properly the first time, because doing it again later is disruptive in a way it is not now.

Contractor access and working hours are set by the community, and a remodel is a daily presence rather than a single delivery. The trade sequence is planned around those windows before the job is quoted, because a schedule that ignores a seven-to-four access rule is not a schedule.
notes: Level access and blocking done once
Detail work rather than structure
Trade sequence built to access hours

goodyear-az.lede: Goodyear houses are young, so a remodel here is nearly always an upgrade rather than a repair.
paras: The structure and the services are modern, which means the work is what the builder did not include: a better kitchen than the standard package, a bathroom reconfigured out of the plan, flooring replaced across the whole ground floor instead of room by room.

Where a house sits on the expansive ground that runs along parts of the city's southern and western edge, movement shows up inside as sticking doors and a cracked tile line. That is worth understanding before new tile goes down, because a floor laid over a moving slab will do the same thing again on the same line.
notes: Upgrade rather than repair
Whole-floor rather than room by room
Movement understood before new tile

queen-creek-az.lede: Queen Creek remodels are mostly recent houses being made to fit the family that grew into them.
paras: The stock is young and generally sound, so the work is space rather than repair: opening a kitchen into a family room, turning a fifth bedroom into a proper office, adding a second laundry. Much of it is recent enough to remain under some form of builder coverage, and we say plainly where something belongs to the original builder rather than to us.

Deliveries are the practical constraint out here. Cabinetry, stone and appliances arrive down a longer road than they do in the inner valley, so the programme is built around fewer, larger deliveries and somewhere on site to store them safely until they are wanted.
notes: Space rather than repair
Builder coverage sorted honestly
Programme built around deliveries

buckeye-az.lede: Buckeye's houses are the newest we remodel, and the brief is usually light and heat.
paras: On open tracts with punishing western exposure, a remodel here has as much to do with glazing, shading and how a room takes the afternoon as it does with cabinetry. We look at which elevation a room sits on before specifying finishes and glass, because a handsome west-facing kitchen nobody can stand in at five o'clock is a failure whatever it cost.

Structurally these houses are straightforward: recent production framing, modern services, few surprises behind the drywall. The programme risk is distance instead. The city is enormous, so trades and deliveries are consolidated rather than shuttled, and the sequence is planned to keep the site working between them.
notes: Glazing and shade in the brief
Few surprises behind new drywall
Trades consolidated over long distances

phoenix-az.lede: Framing in Phoenix means working against whatever the last hundred years left standing.
paras: The city holds every construction era Arizona has had. A 1920s bungalow near the centre has real dimensional lumber, balloon-framed walls and a plaster substrate that does not behave like drywall. A house finished last year north of the 101 has engineered trusses and a load path that runs through particular walls and nowhere else. Which of those we are standing in gets established before anything is cut.

A large share of the mid-century stock is block, and a block house has no stud wall to nail an addition to. The connection is anchored into masonry and the new framing is furred out to meet the existing plane, which is a different detail and a different inspection from timber to timber. Inside a historic overlay the roofline and the street elevation are part of the permit, so the framing is planned around what has to stay.
notes: Block-to-timber connections, anchored not nailed
Historic overlay limits on roofline and elevation
Balloon frame through engineered truss in one city

mesa-az.lede: Most Mesa framing starts against a block wall rather than a stud wall, and that changes the detail.
paras: Post-war ranch and 1970s and 1980s block make up the bulk of the stock. An addition on a masonry house does not tie in by finding a stud: the ledger is anchored into the block, the new wall is set out to meet the existing plane, and the inspection is on the anchors rather than on a nailing pattern. It lays out slower and it does not come loose in ten years.

The newer half is truss-framed on shallow pitches. A truss is an engineered assembly, and cutting one to make room for something is a structural alteration rather than a carpentry decision, so an addition frames alongside and ties in at the ridge instead of through it. Mesa reviews all of it as a City submittal, and we file before the saws come out.
notes: Ledger anchored into block, not nailed
No truss cut without an engineer on it
City of Mesa submittal before demolition

chandler-az.lede: Framing work in Chandler is mostly interior: walls out, headers in, and the roof left where it is.
paras: The houses here are largely sound with dated layouts, so the request is usually to open a kitchen into a living space rather than to add square footage. That turns on one question, which is whether the wall is carrying anything. Under a truss roof the load runs to specific bearing walls and the rest are partitions that can go in an afternoon. Get that the wrong way round and the ceiling will tell you inside a week.

Where a wall is bearing it comes out with a header and posts carrying down to something that can take a point load, which on a slab means knowing what is underneath the bearing point before the wall goes rather than after. Chandler permits structural alterations, and a beam sized by an engineer on paper is what keeps the sign-off uneventful.
notes: Bearing or partition, settled before demolition
Point loads traced down to the slab
Engineered header sizing for the permit

gilbert-az.lede: Gilbert subdivisions repeat, so we usually know what is behind a wall before we open it.
paras: Most of the town went up through the 1990s and 2000s to a handful of builder plans, which means the same elevation carries the same truss layout, the same header sizes and the same bearing lines street after street. We have generally been inside that plan before. That is worth real money to a homeowner: it is the difference between a quote, and a quote plus a day of exploratory demolition to find out what the quote should have said.

It also means the bearing-wall answer is usually available before anyone swings anything. Where an architectural committee governs the community, a framing change that alters an elevation goes to them as well as to the Town, and the two are submitted together. Finding the committee after Gilbert has already approved is a month nobody budgeted for.
notes: Repeating builder plans, known truss layouts
Town permit and architectural review in parallel
No exploratory demolition needed to price it

glendale-az.lede: Glendale framing splits at the 101: real floor joists on one side, slab and trusses on the other.
paras: Around downtown and Catlin Court there is genuine pre-war fabric, some of it on raised foundations with a crawl space and actual floor framing underneath, meaning joists, girders and a rim that can be inspected and repaired. That is uncommon in this valley, and it means a floor problem here has a cause somebody can look at rather than a slab that can only be guessed at.

West of the 101 the stock is 2000s production on slab under engineered trusses, and the framing is extension and reconfiguration rather than repair. The older side carries a second constraint that has nothing to do with carpentry: flood irrigation and mature trees over the work area. We set the framing days around the irrigation turn instead of standing a wall in four inches of water.
notes: Raised foundations and real floor framing downtown
Slab and truss production west of the 101
Framing scheduled around the irrigation turn

scottsdale-az.lede: Scottsdale wants the framing documented before it is built, and on a hillside lot it means it.
paras: Design review here is genuinely enforced, so massing, rooflines and elevations are settled and submitted before a stick is cut. That front-loads the work and it removes the expensive version of the problem, which is a framed wall coming back down because it moved a roof plane the committee had approved on paper.

The hillside and desert-adjacent lots bring stepped foundations, engineered framing packages and disturbed-area limits that govern where a crew is even allowed to stand. West elevations take punishing afternoon sun, and overhang, glazing and shading get decided at framing rather than added afterwards. An overhang is a framing dimension, not a finish.
notes: Elevations approved before anything is cut
Stepped foundations and engineered packages
Overhangs sized at framing, not bolted on later

tempe-az.lede: Tempe lots are too tight to build a wall flat and stand it, so most of it is framed in place.
paras: The city is landlocked and effectively built out, which makes nearly everything infill. On a small lot with neighbours a few feet away there is no ground to lay out a panel and tilt it up, so walls go together stick by stick and the layout has to be right the first time. Where a delivery can stop, what hours the saws run and how the dust is kept on site are part of the framing plan rather than an afterthought.

The stock around the university is 1950s to 1970s ranch, a good deal of it rented and repeatedly altered. We routinely open a wall and find circuits, ducts or a header put in by someone who never pulled a permit. That gets priced honestly at the start rather than discovered halfway through, because a sixty-year-old wall very rarely opens clean.
notes: Framed in place, no room to tilt a panel
Layered unpermitted work inside old walls
Access, hours and dust planned with the layout

peoria-az.lede: Peoria framing changes with the latitude: tie-ins and repairs south, additions north of the 101.
paras: South Peoria is post-war and 1970s block on established streets. Framing there usually ties into masonry, and opening a wall means dealing with whatever the last fifty years put inside it. North of the 101 the ground is master-planned and recent, and the framing is what the production builder left off: a patio enclosure, a casita, a garage conversion, a room extended into a lot that had space for it.

Those northern communities nearly all carry architectural review on top of the City permit. Anything that changes an elevation goes to both, and the two go in together. Sequential submittals are how a month disappears from a schedule for a reason nobody can point at afterwards.
notes: Masonry tie-ins south, additions north
City permit and HOA review filed together
Patio enclosures and garage conversions

surprise-az.lede: Almost every house in Surprise is post-1998, so framing adds to a building rather than repairing one.
paras: The fabric is consistent in a way older valley cities are not: slab-on-grade, engineered truss roofs, stucco over frame. Structural failure is rare. What people want is more house, so a room extended, a patio enclosed, a casita on a lot that was platted with room for one. The framing itself is straightforward; tying it into an engineered roof without touching a truss is the part that takes thought.

Sun City Grand and the other age-restricted communities inside the city set their own contractor access hours and their own architectural rules. A framing programme that ignores a seven-to-four gate is not a programme, so those rules get read before the quote rather than after a date has been promised.
notes: Additions onto sound post-1998 stock
Tied alongside engineered trusses, never through
Age-restricted access hours built into the dates

goodyear-az.lede: In Goodyear the framing question is usually about what the slab underneath it is going to do.
paras: The south and west edges of the city carry expansive soil in places, and a flat lot with poor fall does not forgive a slab placed without thinking about where the water goes. Finished floor level and fall are set against the existing grade at design stage, because framing standing on a slab that moves is not a problem framing can fix.

Above that, Palm Valley, Estrella and the newer tracts are production-built and sound: slab, truss, stucco over frame. Most of what gets framed here is the outdoor living the builder did not include, so extended patios, ramadas and casitas on lots that were platted with room for them and then handed over without them.
notes: Finished floor and fall set before the slab
Expansive soil on the south and west edges
Outdoor living framed onto sound production stock

queen-creek-az.lede: Queen Creek lots are big enough for the framing nobody in the inner valley has the room for.
paras: Shops, detached garages, casitas and covered outdoor space are a large share of what we build here, and the spans are longer than anything in a house. A forty-foot clear shop is an engineered framing package rather than a scaled-up patio cover, and it wants a footing schedule and hold-downs to match. That is a different drawing set and a different inspection from an addition on the back of a tract home.

Parcels toward the edges of town can still be on well and septic, and the utility run out to a new outbuilding is regularly longer than a homeowner expects. We survey that run before quoting: a hundred and fifty feet of trench is a real line item and it belongs on the estimate rather than in a change order.
notes: Long clear spans on engineered packages
Utility runs surveyed before the quote goes out
Detached shops, garages and casitas

buckeye-az.lede: Buckeye has the newest housing in the valley, so nearly all the framing here is shade.
paras: Verrado, Sundance and Festival Ranch are recent production work and structurally sound.
